liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Bertha** (2 reviews): Second set opens with Bertha into Playin' In The Band, then a jam into Ship Of Fools; The Bertha into Playin' opener energizes the second set [12][13]
- **Jack Straw** (1 review): Reviewer calls the Jack Straw jam among the most intense versions they have heard [9]
- **Friend Of The Devil** (1 review): Jerry's voice shines on Friend Of The Devil, reminding the reviewer of the Dead Set version [13]
- **Deep Elem Blues** (1 review): Deep Elem Blues lifted the reviewer out of a funk at their first show [18]
- **The Wheel** (1 review): The Wheel from the second set became the reviewer's favorite song for years [18]
- **Wharf Rat** (1 review): Reviewer says the father liked the gospel section of Wharf Rat and shrugged off its profanity [11]

## The recordings

- **gd1982-04-05.170736.nak700.wagner.miller.clugston.flac2496** (recommended): audience recording; 20 songs; 151 min [1]
- **gd1982-04-05.154912.senn421.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 20 songs; 145 min [3]
- **gd1982-04-05.147439.aud.flac2448**: audience recording; 20 songs; 146 min [5]. Said about its sound: Uploader considers it a nice front-of-board audience recording, despite no known lineage [5]
- **gd1982-04-05.nak700.wagner.miller.90496.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 20 songs; 150 min; rated 3.44/5 by 9 [6]. Said about its sound: Sound improves after Jack Straw [6]
- **gd82-04-05.sennheiser.willy.13612.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 20 songs; 138 min; rated 3.38/5 by 7 [7]. Said about its sound: Audience tape judged very low quality, with typical mid-eighties sound; reviewer downloaded it mainly for Jack Straw; Reviewer calls this the best-sounding copy of the show they have heard, far better than old tapes; Audience recording is better than the reviews suggested, though too close and outside the ideal sweet spot [9][18][19]

## Around the show

- A line dance started by the reviewer's brother wound all the way around The Spectrum [8]
- The show was the reviewer's younger brother Richard's first Grateful Dead concert [8]
- A father in front of the reviewer smoked a pipe and enjoyed the gospel feel of Wharf Rat [11]
- Reviewer recalls a mellow show with smooth playing and nice vocals; a fan nearby said the band sometimes plays until 4 a.m [11]
- Many people never went into the arena, instead dancing up and down outside The Spectrum [15]
- Reviewer's seats were behind the stage, lower down; plenty of elbow room and a very mellow scene [16]
- Reviewer and a friend remember the second set as a train wreck from its start [17]
- The encore was moved to the end of the first set to fit two discs [6]
- Reviewer notes the set is short and Jerry carries more of the load than usual [12]
- Reviewer found the first set great and the second set wacky [16]
- The next night, 4/6, was remembered as one of the best shows; it is slated for Road Trips with some 4/5 [17]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1982-04-05.170736.nak700.wagner.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Bob Wagner; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Bob Wagner's Master Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi 700 (w/ Bass EQ) > Sony TC-D5M (Maxell XLIIS/Dolby B) [1]. Also: A Sennheiser 421 source from Jim Vita supplies a 0:42 patch in Drums [1]
- **gd1982-04-05.154912.senn421.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Jim Vita; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Jim Vita's Master Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser 421 mics > Sony D5M (Maxell XLII C90) [3]. Also: Master recording from Jim Vita, transferred by Charlie Miller, with pitch correction assisted by Joe B. Jones; AndrewF's audience source patches Friend Of The Devil, El Paso, the Tennessee Jed to Little Red Rooster transition, and Drums [3]
- **gd1982-04-05.147439.aud.flac2448**: taped by Unknown via Richie & Rip; transferred by Andrew F.; source: AUD (unknown gear) > MAC > 1st-Gen cassette via Richie & Rip. [5]. Also: Lineage is unknown; this audience source patches Jack Straw and Space from the 13612 source [5]
- **gd1982-04-05.nak700.wagner.miller.90496.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Bob Wagner; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: (FOB) Nakamichi 700 (With Bass EQ) -> Cassette Master (Sony D5M/Maxell DXLIIS/Dolby B) D [6]. Also: Taped from the fourth row with a Sennheiser 441, then cassette master, DAT, and CD [6]
- **gd82-04-05.sennheiser.willy.13612.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience Recording: Sennheiser 441 [7]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Gregg Nixon Grateful Dead: [1982-04-05 The Spectrum, Philadelphia, PA, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1982-04-05-the-spectrum-philadelphia-pa-usa/) [21]
- Poster by Gregg Nixon Grateful Dead: [1982-04-06 The Spectrum, Philadelphia, PA, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1982-04-06-the-spectrum-philadelphia-pa-usa/) [22]
